title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 2nd Congressional District
area: South Jersey, covering Cape May, Cumberland, Salem, and Atlantic counties and parts of Gloucester and Ocean counties, including Atlantic City, Vineland, and the Jersey Shore from Long Beach Island south to Cape May.

context.text: Incumbent Jeff Van Drew ran unopposed in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary. Zack Mullock won a four-way Democratic primary with 39.8% of the vote (17,698 votes), ahead of Tim Alexander (27.4%), Bayly Winder (22.2%), and Terri Reese (10.6%).

Van Drew was first elected to the U.S. House as a Democrat in 2018. On December 19, 2019, he announced he was switching his party affiliation to Republican, after having voted against both articles of impeachment against President Trump the prior day.
context.quote: I believe that this is just a better fit for me. ... This is who I am, it's who I always was, but there was more tolerance of moderate Democrats, of Blue Dog Democrats, of conservative Democrats, and I think that's going away.

context.text: Cook Political Report rated the district's Partisan Voter Index as R+5 as of September 2026; Donald Trump won the district 55.6%–43.0% under the current district lines in the 2024 presidential election.

candidates.name: Jeff Van Drew
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the June 2 Republican primary
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 2nd Congressional District (since 2019)

summary.text: Jeff Van Drew is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 2nd District. A dentist by training, he served as mayor of Dennis Township and in the New Jersey Legislature before his 2018 election to Congress as a Democrat; he switched to the Republican Party in December 2019.

background.text: Born in New York City in 1953; earned a B.S. from Rutgers University and a D.D.S. from Fairleigh Dickinson University Dental School; worked as a family dentist.
Served as mayor of Dennis Township (1994–1995 and 1997–2003), in the New Jersey General Assembly (2002–2007), and in the New Jersey State Senate (2008–2019) before his election to Congress in 2018.

priorities.text: Says he will never support cuts to Social Security, Medicare, or Medicaid for those who are here legally and qualify, and points to his sponsorship of legislation to end federal income tax on Social Security benefits and the bipartisan Social Security Fairness Act.
priorities.quote: I want to be absolutely clear: Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid must always be protected. These programs are lifelines for our seniors, individuals with disabilities, and working families, and I will never support cuts to them.

priorities.text: Says he supports securing the border and expediting deportation of people in the country illegally who have committed crimes, and opposes New Jersey's sanctuary-state policies.
Cites his opposition to offshore wind projects off the South Jersey coast, saying such projects would raise electricity costs and harm the local economy and environment.

positions.summary: Opposes cuts to Medicare and Medicaid benefits for eligible legal residents, but supports empowering Medicare to negotiate lower prescription drug prices and tying U.S. drug prices to other countries' prices, rather than expanding public coverage.

Supports the $165 billion border security package funding border wall construction and DHS detention/deportation resources, and has criticized New Jersey's sanctuary-state policies and local officials who opposed a Newark ICE detention center.

Led opposition to offshore wind projects off the South Jersey coast, holding congressional field hearings against them and working with the Trump administration to halt remaining projects; supports nuclear and natural gas investment instead.

Voted to make the 2017 Trump tax cuts permanent and sponsored legislation eliminating federal income tax on seniors' Social Security benefits, along with new deductions for overtime pay and tipped income.
Says he has stood with Israel since October 7, 2023 and has sponsored legislation to cut federal funding to colleges and universities that allow antisemitic events on campus.
A lifetime NRA member who says he will oppose efforts to restrict Second Amendment rights, including measures similar to past House gun-control bills HR-8 and HR-1112.

record.text: Sponsored the Social Security Fairness Act, bipartisan legislation ending the Windfall Elimination Provision and Government Pension Offset that had reduced Social Security benefits for retired police officers, firefighters, and other public employees; it was enacted into law.

Introduced legislation to eliminate federal income tax on Social Security benefits (announced August 28, 2024); voted July 3, 2025 for a $6,000 senior tax credit that, combined with an enhanced standard deduction, the campaign says ends federal taxes on Social Security income for most seniors.

As a member of the House Judiciary Committee (chairman of a new oversight subcommittee) and the Transportation Committee's Coast Guard and Maritime Subcommittee, secured $425 million for an overhaul of the U.S. Coast Guard Training Center Cape May and worked to secure the FAA William J. Hughes Technical Center's permanent designation as the agency's Center for Advanced Aerospace in South Jersey.

Announced on December 10, 2025 that the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act, as passed by Congress, included $68 million for a new maintenance hangar at the 177th Fighter Wing of the New Jersey Air National Guard in Egg Harbor Township.

First called for a federal takeover of the Atlantic City Housing Authority in November 2023 over unsafe living conditions; HUD notified the agency it was in "substantial default" of the Housing Act of 1937 and took possession of it on July 21, 2025.

Sits on the House Committee on Homeland Security (Transportation and Maritime Security; Intelligence and Counterterrorism subcommittees) and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation; Aviation subcommittees) as of the 2021–2022 session (most recent committee list published by Ballotpedia).

candidates.name: Zack Mullock
candidates.ballotNote: Won a four-candidate June 2 Democratic primary with 39.8% of the vote
candidates.currentRole: Mayor of Cape May, New Jersey (2020–present); Cape May City Council member (2018–present)

summary.text: Zack Mullock is the Mayor of Cape May, New Jersey, elected three times, and previously served eight years on the Cape May City Council. He is a small business owner running as the Democratic nominee for NJ-2 on a platform of affordability, housing, and coastal resiliency.

background.text: Graduated from Wildwood Catholic Academy, earned a bachelor's degree from Mount St. Mary's University in 2008 (where he was class president and a student athlete), and an MBA from Saint Joseph's University in 2010.
Has served on the Cape May City Council for eight years and as Mayor for six years, elected three times.

Helped found and build the Harriet Tubman Museum and the Cape May Point Arts and Science Center, and worked to restore the historic parsonage of the Macedonia Baptist Church; has served on the Atlantic Cape Community College Foundation Board and the United States Coast Guard Community Foundation.

priorities.text: Says he has not raised taxes as mayor in the last seven years while building a new library and fire house and beginning construction of a new police station.
Wants a fairer tax system that holds corporations and the wealthiest accountable, and would focus on lowering the cost of living by addressing hidden fees and taxes on working families.
Would increase federal funding for affordable housing development in South Jersey and support first-time homebuyer assistance programs.
Supports federal investment in coastal resiliency, wetland and dune restoration, and infrastructure to protect South Jersey's beaches, wetlands, and fishing industry.

positions.summary: Wants a fairer tax system that holds corporations and the wealthiest accountable, and would fund an expanded Medicare through fairer corporate taxes.
Would expand Medicare to include dental, vision, and hearing care, protect Medicaid, expand Medicare's power to negotiate drug prices, and work toward a Medicare for All system.
Wants to utilize renewable energy resources and push for federal incentives for energy-efficient homes and businesses.
Would increase federal funding for affordable housing development and support first-time homebuyer assistance programs in South Jersey.

record.text: As Mayor of Cape May, says taxes have not been raised in the last seven years while the city built a new library and fire house and began building a new police station and upgraded lifeguard headquarters.

summary.text: Ramon Mora Jr. is a South Jersey healthcare worker running as an independent, campaigning on affordability, government-accountability reforms, and replacing ICE.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Vineland High School and an associate degree from Atlantic Cape Community College in 2018; has worked in healthcare.
Describes growing up in a Section 8 housing neighborhood and experiencing periods of homelessness, including as a teenager and again around age 20.

priorities.text: Says his top priority is putting people's needs above corporate interests in policymaking.

Lists affordability in housing, education, healthcare, groceries, and utilities as top concerns, along with accountability and transparency reforms across Congress, the courts, and the executive branch.

positions.summary: Supports abolishing and prosecuting ICE and replacing it with what he calls an "American Defense Unit."
Supports abolishing private health insurance in favor of Medicare for All.
